method_card.title: Percentages & Compound Change
steps: Multiplier: increase is 1 + p/100, decrease is 1 − p/100.
One change: multiply once. Compound: multiply by the multiplier to the power n.
Reverse percentage: divide by the multiplier.
method_card.content:
Every percentage change uses a multiplier: a 20% rise is × 1.2, a 15% fall is × 0.85.

Compound change applies the multiplier once per year, so after \(n\) years amount = start \(\times\) multiplier\(^n\). This covers interest, depreciation and population change.

To find the original before a change (reverse percentage), divide by the multiplier instead of multiplying.
method_card.example:
£5000 at 3% compound interest for 4 years.

Multiplier = 1.03. Value = 5000 × 1.03⁴ = 5000 × 1.12550881 = £5627.54 (2 d.p.)

guided_steps.say: 'Percent' means out of 100, so first write 25% as a decimal.

misconceptions.message: 10% means divide by 10, not 100. 350 ÷ 10 = 35.

guided_steps.say: 10% is one tenth. Write it as a decimal first.

guided_steps.done: That rebuilds 350, so 35 is a tenth.

bronze.hint: Find 20% of 60 and add it on, or multiply by 1.2.

misconceptions.message: 12 is the increase, not the new amount. Add it on: 60 + 12 = 72.

guided_steps.say: Increasing keeps the whole £60 and adds 20% on top.

guided_steps.hint: New amount is the old plus the extra.

bronze.hint: Find 15% of 200 and take it off, or multiply by 0.85.

misconceptions.message: 30 is the amount taken off, not the new value. 200 − 30 = 170.

guided_steps.say: Decreasing takes 15% away from the whole 200.

guided_steps.hint: New value is the old minus the slice.

bronze.display: What is the decimal multiplier for a 30% increase?
bronze.hint: An increase adds to 1: think 1 plus the decimal.

misconceptions.message: 0.3 finds 30% OF an amount. To INCREASE you keep the whole (1) and add: 1 + 0.3 = 1.3.

guided_steps.say: An increase keeps all of the original (that is 1 whole) and adds more.

guided_steps.hint: Start from 1 whole, then add the extra.

bronze.display: What is the decimal multiplier for a 5% decrease?
bronze.hint: A decrease takes the decimal off 1.

guided_steps.say: A decrease keeps most of the original and takes a slice off the 1 whole.

bronze.display: A shirt costs £40. It is reduced by 10%. What is the sale price?
bronze.hint: Multiply by 0.9 to pay 90% of the price.

misconceptions.message: £4 is the discount, not the price you pay. Sale price = 40 − 4 = 36.

guided_steps.say: A 10% reduction takes one tenth off the £40.
50% is one half.

guided_steps.done: Two halves make 84, so 42 is half.

silver.display: £2000 earns 5% simple interest per year. How much interest after 3 years?
silver.hint: Simple interest is the same each year: find one year, then times by 3.

misconceptions.message: £2300 is the total in the account. The question asks for the interest only: £300.
£100 is one year's interest. Over 3 years: 3 × 100 = 300.

guided_steps.say: Simple interest pays the same amount every year, worked out on the starting £2000.

guided_steps.hint: Multiply one year by the number of years.
Add the interest to the start.
guided_steps.done: The £300 is the interest earned, which is what was asked.

silver.display: A house bought for £200000 increases in value by 10% per year (compound). What is it worth after 2 years?
silver.hint: Multiply by 1.1 twice, once for each year.

misconceptions.message: Two years of 10% compound is not the same as 20% once. 200000 × 1.1² = 242000, not 240000.
£220000 is the value after 1 year. Apply the 1.1 again: 220000 × 1.1 = 242000.

guided_steps.say: Compound means each year grows on the NEW value, not the start.

guided_steps.hint: Apply it again to the new value.

silver.display: After a 20% increase, a price is £96. What was the original price?
silver.hint: The £96 is 120% of the original, so divide by 1.2.

misconceptions.message: You cannot just take 20% off the new price. The £96 is 120% of the original, so divide by 1.2: 96 ÷ 1.2 = 80.

guided_steps.say: The £96 already INCLUDES the 20% rise, so it is 120% of the original.

silver.display: A car was £15000 new. It is now worth £9600. What percentage has it decreased by?
silver.hint: Divide the amount lost by the original price, then times 100.

misconceptions.message: Percentage change is always out of the ORIGINAL: 5400 ÷ 15000 × 100 = 36, not out of 9600.
64% is what it is still worth. The DECREASE is 100 − 64 = 36.

guided_steps.say: Percentage change is always measured against the ORIGINAL price.

guided_steps.pre: As a percentage of the start: (5400 ÷ 15000) × 100 =

guided_steps.done: That matches the £5400 lost, so 36% is right.

silver.display: A population of 5000 grows by 2% each year (compound). Find the population after 3 years. Give to the nearest whole number.
silver.hint: Multiply by 1.02 three times, or use 1.02 to the power 3.

misconceptions.message: Adding 2% three times to the start gives 5000 × 1.06 = 5300. Compound grows on the new total: 5000 × 1.02³ = 5306.

guided_steps.say: Each year the population grows on the previous year's total.

guided_steps.hint: Apply it to the new total.

silver.display: VAT is 20%. An item costs £84 including VAT. What was the price before VAT?
silver.hint: The £84 is 120% including VAT, so divide by 1.2.

misconceptions.message: You cannot take 20% off the VAT-inclusive price. £84 is 120% of the pre-VAT price, so divide by 1.2: 84 ÷ 1.2 = 70.

guided_steps.say: The £84 already includes 20% VAT, so it is 120% of the price before VAT.

guided_steps.done: Back to £84, so £70 before VAT is right.

silver.display: A laptop depreciates by 25% each year. It cost £800 new. Find its value after 2 years.
silver.hint: Multiply by 0.75 twice, once per year.

misconceptions.message: Losing 25% twice is not losing 50%. Depreciation compounds: 800 × 0.75² = 450, not 800 × 0.5.
£600 is the value after 1 year. Apply 0.75 again: 600 × 0.75 = 450.

guided_steps.say: Losing 25% each year means keeping 75% each year.

guided_steps.hint: Apply it to the new value.

gold.display: After a 15% decrease, a price is £340. What was the original price?
gold.hint: The £340 is 85% of the original, so divide by 0.85.

misconceptions.message: Adding 15% of 340 back on does not reverse a percentage. £340 is 85% of the original, so divide by 0.85: 340 ÷ 0.85 = 400.

guided_steps.say: The £340 is what is left AFTER 15% came off, so it is 85% of the original.

gold.display: £8000 is invested at 4% compound interest. After how many complete years will it first exceed £9000?
gold.hint: Add 4% year by year and count the first total over £9000.

misconceptions.message: After 3 years the total is £8998.91, still just under £9000. It first passes £9000 in year 4.

guided_steps.say: Add 4% each year and watch for the first total over £9000.

guided_steps.hint: Apply it to the new total.
Count the first year the total beats £9000.
guided_steps.done: Year 3 was £8998.91, just short. Year 4 is the first over £9000.

gold.display: A population decreases by 8% each year from 12000. Find the population after 5 years to the nearest whole number.

misconceptions.message: Multiplying the 8% by 5 gives 12000 × 0.6 = 7200. Compound decay keeps 92% each year: 12000 × 0.92⁵ = 7909.

guided_steps.say: A fall of 8% each year means keeping 92% each year for five years.

guided_steps.hint: Dividing by 0.92 steps back a year.
guided_steps.done: That is the year-4 total, and one more × 0.92 returns to 7909.

gold.display: An item is increased by 10% then decreased by 10%. The final price is £495. What was the original price?
gold.hint: Combine 1.1 and 0.9 into one multiplier, then divide the final price by it.

misconceptions.message: A 10% rise then a 10% fall is not zero: 1.1 × 0.9 = 0.99, so the price ends slightly below the start. Divide 495 by 0.99 = 500.

guided_steps.say: A 10% rise then a 10% fall do NOT cancel. Combine the two multipliers first.

guided_steps.hint: Divide the final price by the combined multiplier.

guided_steps.done: Back to £495, so the original was £500.

gold.display: A savings account pays 3.5% compound interest. £6000 is invested. What is the interest earned (not total) after 4 years? Give to the nearest penny.
gold.hint: Find the total with 1.035 to the power 4, then subtract the £6000.

misconceptions.message: £6885.14 is the total in the account. Interest earned = 6885.14 − 6000 = 885.14.
That is simple interest (6000 × 0.035 × 4). Compound gives 6000 × 1.035⁴ − 6000 = 885.14.

guided_steps.say: Grow the money by compounding, then take the £6000 back off to leave just the interest.

guided_steps.hint: 1.035 to the power 4, then × 6000, to the penny.

guided_steps.done: Adds back to the total, so £885.14 interest is right.

problem_bank.bronze_description: Find a percentage of an amount, or a single increase or decrease.
problem_bank.silver_description: Compound growth and depreciation, reverse percentages, and percentage change.
problem_bank.gold_description: Combined changes, reverse compound problems, and 'how many years' questions.

worked_examples.question: A car worth £12000 depreciates by 20% each year. Find its value after 3 years.

bronze.title: Bronze: single percentage of an amount
steps: Percent to decimal: divide by 100. So 30% becomes 0.3.
To increase, add the part on; to decrease, take it off.

silver.title: Silver: compound change and reverse percentages
steps: Multiplier: increase is 1 + p/100, decrease is 1 − p/100. A 4% rise is × 1.04; a 25% fall is × 0.75.
Compound over n years: multiply by the multiplier n times, so × multiplier to the power n.
Reverse: given the amount AFTER a change, divide by the multiplier to get the original.

example.question: A £6000 car loses 15% of its value each year. Its value after 2 years?

gold.title: Gold: multi-step and problem-solving percentages
steps: Combine changes by multiplying the multipliers: a 10% rise then a 10% fall is 1.1 × 0.9 = 0.99, not back to the start.
Reverse a compound change by dividing by the combined multiplier.
For 'how many years until', apply the multiplier year by year and count when the total passes the target.

opener.display: A £20 hoodie is in a '20% off' sale. Work out what you actually pay.

steps.hint: Take the discount off the price.

steps.say: You just did a percentage decrease. There is a one-step shortcut: paying 80% of the price means × 0.8, and 20 × 0.8 = 16. That multiplier, 0.8, is the whole method. Every question in this lesson is really 'find the multiplier, then multiply'.

steps.done: Gone in one multiply. That is the shortcut.

silver.display: A £1200 bike loses 20% of its value each year. Find its value after 2 years.

steps.hint: Apply it to the new value.
steps.done: Each year works on the latest value.

gold.display: £2500 is invested at 4% compound interest per year. Find the interest earned after 3 years, to the nearest penny.

steps.say: Grow the money first, then strip out the original to leave just the interest.

steps.hint: 1.04 to the power 3, then × 2500, to the penny.
Subtract the money you started with.
steps.done: Interest is the growth on top of the original.
Adds back to the total, so £312.16 is the interest.
